summary: This Wikipedia article covers the Money in the Bank ladder match and its briefcase contract, which lets the holder cash in for a title match within one year. It recounts notable contract holders and cash-ins, including Cena, Edge, Bryan and Rollins, and records that the first match was held at WrestleMania 21 in 2005. It also describes the 2018 Money in the Bank pay-per-view, which was dual-branded and held at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois.
one_line: Overview of WWE's Money in the Bank ladder match, its briefcase contract rules, notable cash-ins, and the 2018 dual-branded event.
key_facts: The Money in the Bank contract is valid for one year.
The briefcase holder can cash in the contract at the date, place, and time of their choosing.
Briefcase holders are dubbed 'Mr. Money in the Bank' or, for women, 'Ms. Money in the Bank'.
All briefcase holders have successfully defended and cashed in the contract except Mr. Kennedy.
John Cena, Damien Sandow, and Baron Corbin are the only Money in the Bank contract holders to cash in and fail to gain a championship.
John Cena has had the contract cashed in against him three times, by Edge, Rob Van Dam, and Damien Sandow.
Edge, Daniel Bryan, and Seth Rollins are the only contract holders given a title shot without cashing in the contract for it.
The 2018 Money in the Bank pay-per-view took place on June 17, 2018, at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois.
The 2018 event was dual-branded, involving both the Raw and SmackDown brands, for the first time since 2011.
The 2018 event included one male match and one female match.
The first Money in the Bank ladder match was contested in 2005 at WrestleMania 21.
Chris Jericho invented the Money in the Bank ladder match in kayfabe.
Edge won the inaugural Money in the Bank ladder match, which was at the time exclusive to Raw wrestlers.
The Money in the Bank pay-per-view debuted in July 2010 and featured two ladder matches, one each for the WWE Championship and World Heavyweight Championship contracts.
Rollins received a title shot at the 2015 Royal Rumble in a triple threat match also involving Cena and champion Brock Lesnar.
